sentences.text:
2. The case of the prosecution is that, the petitioner/accused No.1 subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty, both mentally and physically, and also demanded to bring money from parental home,
and the other accused abused the defacto complainant with reference to her caste.

3. The parties are present before this Court and have filed an application for compounding under Section 320 read with Section 482 of Cr.P.C stating that the parties have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves and their marriage has been dissolved mutually in M.C.NO.4636/2023 and a sum of Rs.5,50,000/- is paid as permanent alimony to the defacto complainant, the receipt of which is duly acknowledged by the defacto complainant who is present before this Court.
4. The second respondent/defacto complainant has no objection to quash the impugned proceedings.
5. The application is placed on record.

Though the offences alleged are cognizable and non compoundable, however having regard to the fact that the parties have amicably settled the dispute among themselves, and the second respondent having no objection to quash the impugned proceedings, it would be a futile exercise, if the petitioners are subjected to trial, since the probability of conviction of the petitioners is remote and bleak in view of the settlement.
Therefore, the continuation of the proceedings against the petitioners will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. Criminal petition is allowed.
ii.
The impugned proceedings in Spl.C.No.502/2019 on the file of LXX Addl. City Civil and Special Judge, Bengaluru is hereby quashed.
